prior_importants.description: In a session, a dirty `package.json` (staged, unstaged or untracked) now makes the pre-commit run the whole suite. `vitest list --changed` returns every test once a changed file matches `forceRerunTriggers`, and a single test slot is held for the full run.

findings.description: `leadingOptions` ends the option list at the first argument that doesn't start with `-`. That argument can be the value of a runner option rather than a file. If `--related` comes with a separately valued option such as `-t sum` or `--reporter dot`, the `--` the CLI keeps lands after the cut. `relatedArgs` then passes it on to vitest, and vitest files the paths under `options['--']`. `vitest related --passWithNoTests` sees no file and exits 0 with nothing run. If the valued option comes before `--related`, related mode is never detected, and `--related` goes to the project's own test command.

`runSessionTest`'s JSDoc still opens with "the project's test command with `args` after it", but with `--related` before the files it ignores `req.command` and runs `RELATED_TEST_COMMAND` (`pnpm exec vitest related ...`); add a clause naming the swap so a maintainer doesn't assume `command` is always the one spawned.

`relatedMode(args)` is a one-line wrapper, `leadingOptions(args).includes(RELATED_FLAG)`, with a single caller (the ternary in `runSessionTest`) and a JSDoc that restates its body; general.md §Inline by default asks to inline it as `leadingOptions(req.args).includes(RELATED_FLAG)`.
